subject: Performance evaluation & close timeline — streaming TTFT plan
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Performance evaluation & close timeline — streaming TTFT plan

Hi Elaine / James,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Per our closing checklist I’ve drafted a short mutual action plan (MAP) focused on the streaming TTFT and concurrency evaluation that your acceptance team asked for. The goal is to validate p50/p95/p99 TTFT and streaming latency under the target concurrency profile so we can sign the SOW by the end of July.

High-level acceptance criteria (proposed):
- TTFT (chat streaming): p50 <= 180ms, p95 <= 420ms, p99 <= 800ms for single-turn messages at baseline prompt length (200 tokens).
- Streaming per-token latency: p50/p95 targets called out for first-token and subsequent tokens.
- Sustained concurrency: 150 concurrent active streams (simulated users) for 30-minute windows without >1% error rate.
- Throughput sanity: end-to-end tokens/sec and aggregated TTF throughput within 15% of benchmark baseline.

Attached is an operational evaluation plan that includes: test vectors, sample prompts, harness configs, and responsibilities. Key asks from ClearMed: confirm the two production locales (us-west-2 + us-east-1), provide the set of 20 representative prompts (redacted patient examples are fine), and designate an engineering contact who can accept a temporary test token and run the smoke run on your side.

Timeline (proposed MAP milestones):
- 2027-06-23: Finalize test vectors & locale confirmation (owner: ClearMed).
- 2027-06-25: Redwood will run baseline tests and share p50/p95/p99 dashboards and raw logs (owner: Redwood performance).
- 2027-06-29: Joint validation run (both sides run coordinated loadgen) + review session.
- 2027-07-02: Buffer for remediation and follow-up tests.
- 2027-07-09: Final sign-off on performance acceptance (target).

Owners we’ve proposed:
- Redwood (performance lead): Marcus Lin — will coordinate benchmarks, provide load generator configs and dashboard links.
- Redwood (platform/ops): Monica Patel — network and region configuration, temporary tokens, and log access.
- ClearMed (eng): please confirm.

Practical notes:
- We plan to use our streaming harness (continuous chunked responses) to capture first-byte TTFT and per-token latencies. The attached loadgen config also contains the pattern to simulate interleaved user typing and long sessions.
- We’ll provide scripts to reproduce tests (see test-scripts.tar.gz attachment) and an initial summary table after the baseline run.

Please review the plan attached and the proposed timeline; if the milestones look good I’ll add the joint validation session to calendars (30–45 minute block).

Best,
Sofia
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Elaine / James — quick follow-up from the Redwood performance side with more detail on the test configurations and the cold/warm profile James requested.

Test configuration summary (details in loadgen-config.yaml):
- Cold-start profile: reload model per-session, clear KV cache between sessions. Target distribution: 30% of sessions to cold-start.
- Warm profile: reused instances with KV cache warm; 70% of sessions.
- Message lengths: baseline 200 tokens, stress tests at 400 and 800 tokens.
- Concurrency profile: steady-state 150 concurrent active streams, spike windows up to 300 concurrent streams for no more than 10 minutes to validate graceful degradation.
- Metrics captured: first-byte TTFT, first-token latency, per-token inter-arrival, end-to-end tail latencies (p50/p95/p99), error rate, and CPU/GPU utilization traces.

Run plan:
- 2027-06-25 09:00 PT: Redwood baseline run (we’ll push results to shared Drive, link in the MAP).
- 2027-06-29 10:00 PT: Joint validation — both sides run loadgen and share telemetry in real-time.

Telemetry/PII note: our harness will only capture timing and request metadata (request id, model variant, sequence length, token counts). No prompt content or PHI will be transmitted in logs. We’ll supply a short JSON schema of the telemetry fields ahead of the tests (attached: loadgen-config.yaml contains field names).

Attachment: loadgen-config.yaml (contains command-line flags and the seed prompt set). Also included small helper scripts in test-scripts.tar.gz to make reproduction straightforward. If you prefer, we can run the baseline and provide a sanitized event stream for your audit prior to the joint run.

Marcus
Performance Engineering — Redwood Inference
